A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PLMC convergence-analysis work. All 22 pages of each version, including Table 1, equations, and Appendices A–H, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical convergence bounds and proofs. Table 1 compares analytical complexity guarantees; neither the main text nor appendices report original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical results and proof appendices. Its added discussion reports a guarantee attributed to concurrent work, with no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 retains the same overdamped and underdamped PLMC recurrences, Bernoulli midpoint selection, and cheap interpolation. The double-midpoint implementation newly mentioned in Remark 4 belongs to cited work.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or instantiated benchmark tasks. The strongly log-concave sampling problem remains unchanged; the additional citation introduces no evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version contains empirical baseline evaluations. Table 1 retains the same LMC, RLMC, and PLMC comparisons; the concurrent double-midpoint method is discussed but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols. PLMC parameter prescriptions are unchanged; the newly mentioned low-friction regime describes concurrent work, not a revised setting for this paper.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness experiments, sensitivity studies, or empirical case studies are added or removed. Appendices A–H retain the same technical lemmas and proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained probabilistic moment bounds are theoretical analysis, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: There are no original empirical results in either version, and Table 1's complexity bounds are unchanged. The added rate in Remark 4 is an attributed literature comparison, not a new PLMC outcome.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, theorems, corollaries, coupling arguments, and proofs in Sections 4–6 and Appendices A–H match after accounting for citation renumbering and pagination. Remark 4 adds no derivation or revision to this analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 2.4, and discussion retain the claims of cubic improvement in accuracy dependence over LMC and Wasserstein convergence beyond strong-L2 complexity lower bounds. The best-known accuracy-dependence claim is retained.

C2.justification: Remark 4 adds comparison context by specifying that the concurrent guarantee concerns KL error, low friction, and double-midpoint RLMC. The existing strong-versus-weak error interpretation and limitations concerning dimension and condition-number dependence remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithmic details and parameter prescriptions are unchanged, including the reference to Kandasamy and Nagaraj for efficient implementation. No code/data access information, hardware specifications, or runtime disclosures are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Altschuler, Chewi, and Zhang's Shifted Composition IV as reference [2], citing it in the introduction, Section 2.3, and Remark 4. The remark attributes an O-tilde(κ^(5/6)d^(5/3)/ϵ^(2/3)) rate for KL ≤ ϵ² to this concurrent work. Existing cited works are retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds two sentences to Remark 4, expands several citation lists, and updates the arXiv version/date text. Section order, terminology, and almost all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Text reflow changes spacing and page breaks, including moving Section 7 from PDF page 9 to page 10 and shifting appendix content. Table 1 retains its structure and placement; no figures are added.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves research positioning by acknowledging concurrent underdamped RLMC work and specifying its guarantee, metric, and friction regime in Remark 4. This supplies useful context for assessing the retained novelty claim. The method, principal guarantees, and proofs remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
